active_layer_context.note: Published summary context; does not mean each modality can resolve both endpoints.

literature_characteristics.reported_capability: better-than-10-nm depth profiling under suitable sample, standards and instrument conditions
literature_characteristics.response_kernel_status: must be calibrated for the Pd/Ti specimen

literature_characteristics.reported_capability: 2-5-nm near-surface resolution in suitable smooth samples; degradation with depth due to energy straggling
literature_characteristics.response_kernel_status: not a D measurement without a distinct isotope-sensitive method

literature_characteristics.reported_capability: 10-nm a-C:D reference layers used to study resolution; apparent profile broadened by overlayer thickness and matrix
variable-energy Makhov implantation profiles; tens of nm to few hundred nm at low energies, broadening with energy
caveats: depth kernel is distributed, not a point

literature_characteristics.reported_capability: 2025 Pd study discusses approximately 50-micrometre spatial resolution
caveats: this is spatial/lateral resolution, not depth resolution
literature_characteristics.response_kernel_status: keep lateral PSF separate from depth response

literature_characteristics.reported_capability: electron penetration depths about 60-458 nm over 4-15 kV in the reported Pd study
caveats: effective defect metric may include vacancies, voids, cracks and other defects
literature_characteristics.response_kernel_status: requires its own electron-transport / thermal-absorbance kernel

kernels.meaning: synthetic broad response; not a real instrument profile

synthetic_example.note: These weights are artificial test inputs only; no actual SIMS/NRA/PAS/ZEM response matrices are asserted.

limitations: Literature resolution values are method- and specimen-specific, not guaranteed for PdD/TiD under irradiation.
Depth response and lateral spatial resolution are separate dimensions.
Hydrogen-specific NRA reaction 1H(15N,alpha gamma)12C does not directly measure deuterium.
The response operator is a linear weighted-average scaffold and does not yet model non-linear sputtering, isotope cross-talk, positron trapping, scattering or measurement noise.
